programme.title: Iceland - On Top of the World
programme.desc: A scenic expedition through majestic volcanoes, seething geysers, powerful waterfalls, threatening fjords and almighty glaciers. Hardly any other country offers such a variety of spectacular forces of nature! We will give you an insight on how it can be that the people of a small, distant island with only a fraction of sunlight in some months are happier than the people in more sun-blessed countries.

programme.title: mareTV: Sweden's High Coast
programme.desc: Sweden's Höga Kusten (High Coast) has been rising by almost one centimetre per year since the last ice age 10,000 years ago. This has created a hilly Baltic Sea landscape on the Gulf of Bothnia with small and large islands. Untouched nature, dense forests and energetic, rather idiosyncratic islanders have plenty of room there. Every year at the end of August a biting stench mixes with the fresh Baltic Sea breeze. For weeks the so-called sour herring, Swedish: Surströmming, is fermented in brine. Ruben Madsen is a producer of surströmming and an absolute connoisseur. In his wooden hut on the island of Ulvön he puts the herring in according to a traditional recipe. At the start of the season, the cans are opened for the first time. Lovers of the "stinky fish" then come from all over the world to taste the now world-famous delicacy in cans. Opening the cans of "rotten fish" is considered internationally as a test of courage, people film themselves doing so, the inhabitants of the High Coast can only smile about it.

programme.title: Sri Lanka - Tropics, temples and tea plantations
programme.desc: Sri Lanka stands for colourful diversity in all respects. If it's spirituality or Ayurveda you're looking for, here it is. Adventurers and nature lovers can also satisfy their needs here. No one must travel far to discover exotic worlds on this drop-shaped tropical island. "mareTV" delves into the day to day lives of the is-landers, some of whom pursue the most unusual pro-fessions: Uditha Lakmaal is a palm tree climber. He harvests the sap of the trees, known as palm wine, by climbing to the top of them. Sri Lankan stilt fishermen now actually have very little to do with fish and func-tion more as models receiving payment from tourists for acting the part. Anulawathie runs a small floating hoop business, offering car inner tubes for adults and tuk-tuk tubes for children. Different varieties of tea can be found on Herman Gunaratnes tea plantation. Just four carefully selected women are allowed to harvest the exclusive white tea grown there. Each tea leaf is cut individually from the bush by gloved hands and with golden scissors.

programme.title: Wild Faces of the Andes
programme.desc: The Andes are the biggest mountain range in the world. Peaks of up to 7000 metres in height, do not only offer an imposing view, but also influence the climate by being the drainage and meteorological divide.

programme.title: Germany's Mystic Forest
programme.desc: 2.000 rivers and streams dig deep into the underground and transport their water into reservoirs or "Germany's Wild Amazon", the Wupper. These forests and rivers, together with heathlands and moors, are home to a diverse fauna. Martens, badgers, wild boars, hares, roe deer, and red deer, even black grouse and hazel deer find shelter in these parts. Wolves also have a dominant presence, not to mention those who live underground, such as lizards, bats, and snakes. Accompany us on a journey where we explore every corner of this rugged land. Climb underground into the Bergisches Land, through the vast hidden cave systems that sprawl far beneath the forests. There is also much to be discovered in the water, dive with us in crystal clear streams and rivers with their diverse flora and fauna.

programme.title: Magical Moors
programme.desc: Wide open heaths, windswept and barren in winter, are transformed into wonderful carpets of white, fluffy cotton grass in summer. Large bears and wolves roam alongside delicately fluttering butterflies, the bubbling calls of black grouse and the enchanting trills of the great snipe. Moors, bogs and wetlands can be found all over in Europe. Everyone has at least heard about this habitat but most know little about it. It is an ancient yet largely unknown set of landscapes that is full of enchanting surprises. On a warm spring day, poisonous adders emerge from hiding to perform their impressive mating dance. As dusk falls, snipe gather on traditional leks, leaping and singing to impress the opposite sex. And deep down in the boggy marshes, glittering emeralds of sticky dew lure insects into the deadly arms of meat-eating plants. Magical Moors captures the quiet beauty of a spectacular landscape, and its often elusive wildlife, in stunning detail.

programme.title: Masai Mara: The Big Hunt
programme.desc: When food supply in the Serengeti dwindles, the Masai Mara is a paradise for predators. As the black wildebeests, gazelles, zebras and antelopes make their yearly trip from the south of the Serengeti to the north, nature’s best laid trap, the Mara River in Kenya is waiting ahead. Captivating shots filmed under water show how crocodiles prepare for the Big Hunt while other predators lurk on the banks awaiting their bounty. The biggest problems for the migratory animals are the Mara and the Tarek River, where they have to put their lives at risk to get to the other side. A great number of them die as they jump into the river and break their legs, while others are carried away by the drift or drown. Those who are not victims of the river itself risk falling prey to the crocodiles. We entered this unchartered territory, the crocodile domain by heading under water. Follow these predators in and around their habitat and watch prides of lions map out their game plan. In slow-motion, we show you the final showdown between predator and prey. Will it be a successful hunt or will the hoofed animals persevere?

programme.title: Penguin City - South Georgia
programme.desc: In the middle of the Antarctic Ocean, an entire mountain range arises from the water: South Georgia, the nursery of the Antarctic. Hundreds of thousands of penguins, elephant seals, fur seals and their young overcrowd the beaches. The rough weather and the extremely difficult access to the island cause filmmaking to be an endeavor requiring much of the film crew around Roland Gockel and Rosie Koch and the state of the art cameras. A lot of patience and sensitivity over a period spanning some five years now offers unknown and poignant insights into the life of the King Penguins on South Georgia Island

programme.title: Over the Islands of Africa
programme.desc: Photographer Matthias Ziegler is an Africa specialist. He has visited nearly every country on the continent on assignments for international agencies. Zanzibar, however, is new territory for him. He's come to the former slave island for a photo book – and this time he's not alone. To see the Tanzanian archipelago from the air, he has enlisted the services of ultralight pilot Richard Meredith-Hardy of England to fly him around in his FIB, or flying inflatable boat. Perfect conditions for an adventurous journey: as a world champion ultralight pilot, Richard and his FIB can take off and land practically anywhere – in theory.

programme.title: Over the Islands of Africa
programme.desc: Renaud Van Der Meeren is a photographer and paramotor pilot. With his motorised parachute he goes on expeditions to the remotest corners on earth to photograph people and landscapes from the air. Renaud wanted to be a jet pilot, studied music at the Sorbonne, became a ski instructor, model and photographer's assistant before he found happiness in his current vocation. He especially likes to do his job in Mauritius – nowhere else does he find so many motifs as on the "sweetest pearl in the Indian Ocean". This time he's working on a photo book about Mauritius – by land, by water and in the air.

programme.title: Over the Islands of Africa
programme.desc: Spirits, Kings, Lemurs – Madagascar treats Ami to a multitude of new impressions and spectacular pictures. Director Christian Schidlowski and his team accompanied her on her trip.

programme.title: Over the Islands of Africa
programme.desc: Along with photographer Rui Camilo, we travel to the West African island nation of Sao Tomé and Príncipe - in search of images that will capture the soul of this small and beautiful country.

programme.title: Over the Islands of Africa
programme.desc: Cape Verde – the islands of Saudade, of longing. For Stéphane and Richard it was a journey full of adventure, unforgettable encounters and magnificent photographs. Director Christian Schidlowski and his team accompanied them on their trip.

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: Chasing Quakes
programme.desc: Europe has experienced catastrophic earthquakes – even though the 'old continent' is not the most notorious region on Earth for strong quakes, the danger from below is very real. Autumn 2016 tragedy strikes north-central Italy. A series of four earthquakes cracks a mountain and flattens a historic town.

programme.title: Meteor Menace
programme.desc: On February 15th, 2013, out of the blue, a meteorite exploded in the earth’s atmosphere above the Russian region of Chelyabinsk. The event is a reminder of the ever-present 'Meteor Menace' and the need to understand more about these missiles from outer space.

programme.title: The Sun - Inferno in the Sky
programme.desc: On July 23rd, 2012, a massive eruption on the sun hurls a colossal cloud of solar matter into space. It’s the most severe sunstorm in 150 years. Fortunately, the Earth is not in the direct path of this solar ejection. But it’s only a matter of time before a violent solar storm hits us. When these clouds of charged matter reach our planet, they can wreak havoc in electrical systems.

programme.title: Moon, The: Our Gateway To The Universe
programme.desc: We are on the verge of a new age of exploration: besides the plans of NASA and other space agencies, over the next years also privately financed teams are going to send unmanned vehicles to the Moon. The goal is to find a cheap and efficient way to travel there on a regular basis, and in the long term to build a permanent human base.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto the dangerous roads of Afghanistan's Hindu Kush Mountains, the infamous Moloto Road in South Africa, along the vertiginous slopes of the Bolivian Andes and other "roads of death" in India, Georgia and the Ivory Coast

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these autoroutes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured! With the two-part "Death Roads - On the Road at the Limit," phoenix offers a documentary road movie along the world's most dangerous car routes.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these car routes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are much more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto dangerous roads in New Zealand, Scotland and Australia for phoenix.

programme.title: New Life
programme.desc: Baby animals beguile with their innocent charm. But while some remain harmless, others have a deep-rooted instinct. It may take weeks or months of training to hone their skills. Their landscapes and lifestyles maybe very different, but these babies are born to hunt.

programme.title: New Life
programme.desc: In a land of dangers, plant-eating animals are always at risk, and never more so than at the time of their birth; out on the open they are vulnerable and there are few places to hide. But luckily some are born to run …

programme.title: New Life
programme.desc: It's a water world and life couldn't survive without it. And thanks to it, a mind blowing diversity of creatures thrive beneath the surface. Born to enjoy the riches underwater they must master their body's adaptations, learn to find food, to escape danger and above all become expert swimmers! Whether it's in rivers, on beaches or in the deep ocean, all must overcome the obstacles and fulfil their destiny, all are born to swim! Of all the habitats on earth, the ocean is perhaps the most challenging. Here salt, temperatures, currents and predators can make life difficult; it's not an obvious place to want to bring up your babies… But even in these waters generation after generation beats the odds. They have overcome the challenges and become some of the most beautiful and graceful of creatures. But any baby born to swim has a lot to learn… All over the world there are creatures born to swim, and though humans are not, we seem determined to join them. Perhaps we are envious of their grace. Maybe we are all water babies at heart

programme.title: Kids In Prison
programme.desc: From inside juvenile prison, teenager Shawn discusses his life as a gay prisoner inside one of America's largest juvenile prisons. Shawn talks about when he decided to come out, what life was like in his old community, and how it is to be a gay teen locked inside a juvenile prison with 400 other teen boys. This episode also features scenes with a juvenile corrections officer and juvenile prison counselor who are called to a unit due to two teen boys fighting over the affections of another teen boy, and how prison staff handle issues of this kind with incarcerated youth.

programme.title: Kids In Prison
programme.desc: Our cameras capture two cell extractions -- one "voluntary" and one "involuntary." The "involuntary" extraction is a rare look inside a maximum-security juvenile prison as juvenile prison correctional officers make the decision to forcibly remove a teen from his cell when the teen refuses to give back a broom he has inside. A female officer tries verbal de-escalation first, to no avail. The teen is then removed by a tactical team of 7 officers wearing riot gear. In the second half of this episode, we see officers converse with a teenager in an isolation cell who requests to be put in the "time out" chair in order to get control of his anger.

programme.title: Fatal Crimes
programme.desc: Jennifer Cave's body is found by her stepfather in an Austin condo. What follows is a manhunt that leads authorities across the Mexican border. Inconclusive evidence leaves many to wonder if police have arrested the right suspect.

programme.title: Cruise Ship Killers
programme.desc: Sadie, a professor's assistant goes missing at sea near the end of a long voyage. And clues to her disappearance are detailed in a diary discovered in her cabin. How did she disappear? And does anyone on board know what happened to her.

programme.title: Classic Ride
programme.desc: In the 1950s, companies like Tatra from Czechoslovakia introduced advanced, even pioneering automobiles. The clientele was exclusive, which is why now these streamlined cars are big rarities. We tracked down the owner of a 1937 Tatra T87.

programme.title: Classic Ride
programme.desc: The Porsche 911 Targa with its lightweight construction is an iconic car. Also: the Lotus Seven Twin Cam SS is more pf a race than a road car. And: the 1930 Bentley Blower and the dainty British roadster, the Sunbeam Tiger.

programme.title: Classic Ride
programme.desc: The 1967 Ford Fairlane GTA in NASCAR trim. Also: the 1995 Chrysler 300 C was the most powerful production vehicle in the US. And: the 1949 Cadillac Series 62 convertible set new standards in terms of luxury.

programme.title: Classic Ride
programme.desc: The 1947 Triumph 1800 Roadster provides space for 5 fresh air fans. Also: Le Jog, the toughest classic car rally in Europe. A German women's team takes on the challenge in their VW Iltis. And: a charming oldie, the 1919 Wolseley Stellite.

programme.title: Facel Vega Facellia
programme.desc: In the late 1950s, the Facel Vega Facellia was designed to compete with Porsche and Alfa Romeo and open a new market segment for the fledgling French luxury car company.

programme.title: BMW M3
programme.desc: In the late 80s BMW brought a car onto the market which carried true racing genes. Initially conceived as a homologation model for the German Touring Car Championship, it developed into being one of the world's hottest street sports car. Whenever its name is mentioned, car fans feel goosebumps - even today: the BMW M3.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: At the "Day of Thunder" in Magdeburg, Germany, two- and four-wheelers take part in Europe's most famous 1/8 mile race.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: Already in the eighth season of the German Race Wars, visitors from over 20 countries make their pilgrimage to the big event. And: The Mini John Cooper Works is the racing version of the Bavarian racer. Arden turns it into the Arden Mini AM 3.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: For BMW tuner Manhart Racing, the Nurburgring Nordschleife is the ideal place to celebrate its 25th anniversary. As part of the Track Days, customers and interested parties will have the opportunity to get to know the Manhart models.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: Once a year, car tuning fans from all over the country meet at Neue Messe Dresden for the XS CarNight. On 35,000 square metres automotive dreams can be admired there while the lights go out outside.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: Unlike the countless Show & Shine car meetings, at the Rust'n'Roll the older means the better. Only when the vehicles look really old and are as rusty as possible are they considered beautiful.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: The NitrolympX is a motor sport event that was first held in Hockenheim in 1986. With about 30,000 spectators and around 300 participants, it is the largest international drag race event in Europe.

programme.title: A tuned Beetle!
programme.desc: It looks like a Volkswagen Beetle from the Seventies. But with contemporary tuning, 90 horse power and 112 mph top speed, it promises unlimited driving pleasure.

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: We took the Ferrari 458 Italia for a spring ride around Lake Starnberg. Also: a test drive of BMW's 6 series convertible at the Table Mountain in South Africa. And: the Chevrolet Orlando family van.

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: Audi built only 333 units of its GT model. We tested the everyday use compatibility of the R8 GT. In addition: the Mazda MX5, the most popular roadster in the world. And: the Mercedes-AMG GT3.

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: More efficiency, less weight and more sportiness is what Audi promotes in order to win the race against BMW and Mercedes with their A6 2.0 TDI. Also: Patrick Dempsey and his racing team at the Grand Am Rolex Sportscar GT series.

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: We put the Wiesmann MF5 at the racetrack in Spa-Francochamps in the Belgian Ardennes to the test. Also: Audi A1 vs. Mini Cooper RS. And: the GT Academy 2011 qualifying rounds.

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: The Nurburgring 24 Hours is considered the most difficult long distance race in motor sports. Volkswagen set themselves this challenge with a car built especially for this occasion, their Golf 24.

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: The Mercedes-Benz SL 65 AMG is the ultimate German muscle car in a tailor-made suit. Also: the Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG, the Formula 1 safety car. And: BMW's 6 series models.

programme.title: Jaguar D-Type
programme.desc: The high-achiever at the 24 hours of Le Mans. The Jaguar D-Type won the toughest endurance race in the world three times in a row.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The emphatically sporty cars and motorbikes of BMW are equally successful with customers and in racing. However, the former aircraft engine manufacturer's entry into automobile production threatened to fail at an early stage.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The Porsche 550 Spyder is small and fast, but only 140 units were built. It was Porsche's first racing sports car and laid the foundation for the German manufacturer to be considered a force in car racing today.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Racing has been a matter of the heart for Ford for over 100 years. Henry Ford already wins the first race with his first car. Thousands of other victories were to follow.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The development of engineering at BMW has always been closely linked to motorsport. Racing has always played a decisive role in shaping the brand and setting the pace for its future.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: In the 1980s and 90s, Porsche races from victory to victory. A McLaren with Porsche engine wins the Formula 1 World Championship three times. In Le Mans in 1982, Porsche starts an unbelievable winning streak with the new 956/962 prototype.

programme.title: Glas 1700 GT
programme.desc: The Glas GT looks like a Ferrari, but comes from the province of Lower Bavaria in Germany. In the early 1960s it was one of the few German sports cars.

programme.title: Peugeot 205 Turbo 16
programme.desc: Peugeot released this classic, all wheel drive monster for one purpose only: It should bring the World Rally Championship to France. The Peugeot 205 Turbo 16 shook up the rally world in the 80s.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: What a joy it is when elegance meets extraordinary performance! The Maserati Quattroporte, the Kelleners BMW GranCoupe and Porsche's 911 4S embody the perfect melange. We took a closer look at these prime examples of power combined with style.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Two weeks before the start of the famous 24 hours of Le Mans race, all teams are busy testing their cars on the traditional long distance track in France. Bad weather, accidents and a lot of tension, we documented the official test days in Le Mans 2013.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: The Porsche 911 shows stylistic modesty like no other sports car in the world. It doesn't boast, avoids any loud appearance and puts form over function. We explored the history behind this iconic sports car and the reason why it has been so successful for more than 50 years. In addition: Porsche's Turbo S model, the traditional top model of the brand's 911 production series.

programme.title: Volvo Laplander 6x6
programme.desc: More extremes are always possible. Volvo's Laplander army vehicle has 6 wheels, 3 axles and provides space for at least 12 soldiers.

programme.title: Aston Martin DB11 - The first turbocharged Aston Martin
programme.desc: Aston Martin are pursuing future success with their DB11 model. Apart from the beautiful new design, turbochargers are used for the first time, but, not to worry, the magnificent V12 remains in place.

programme.title: Chevrolet Corvair
programme.desc: Despite a production number of nearly 1.4 million units the Chevrolet Corvair is virtually unknown in Europe. It was innovative, efficient, modern and cheap. Nevertheless, it was slandered, torn apart and later reviled.

programme.title: Stunt Heroes
programme.desc: This episode features Action Concept's stunt highlights from all previous specials, from exciting car stunts to meticulously choreographed fight scenes and even some snowmobile shootout action.

programme.title: Stunt Heroes
programme.desc: This time, an industrial site is the scene for the stunt extravaganza. The Stunt Heroes' objective: jump through a truck trailer with a car. As usual with such risky car stunts, careful planning, preparation, timing and precision are of the essence.

programme.title: Stunt Heroes
programme.desc: In a race between a dump truck and a car, man and machine are brought to their limits. Stuntman Stefan receives a load of gravel for his birthday, instead of confetti.

programme.title: Audi MTM S8 Talladega R
programme.desc: The Audi S8 Plus is by no means underpowered, but it is and remains faithful to this model series' understatement. Those who want more power can get a boost from MTM.

programme.title: Ferrari California T
programme.desc: The Ferrari California T has a lot of Italian passion and elegant lines to offer. Super sports car cabriolets are popular all over the world. It is no wonder that more and more manufacturers are 'opening up'.

programme.title: BMW Active Hybrid 7
programme.desc: With the Active Hybrid 7, unlike with its predecessor bearing the same model name, BMW now banks on a full hybrid, which can also be driven solely with electric power.

programme.title: Classic Races
programme.desc: The Pikes Peak Hill Climb is a rather unique type of car race in the mountains of Colorado, USA. It's exciting, tough and dangerous, and in 1987, two-time world rally champion Walter Röhrl took his Audi Sport Quattro S1 to the top.

programme.title: Classic Races
programme.desc: In the 1930s the famous Silver Arrows by Auto Union that were designed by Ferdinand Porsche celebrated great successes at the European Drivers' Championship and several Grand Prix races despite the strong competition by Mercedes-Benz.

programme.title: Classic Races
programme.desc: The International Championship for Manufacturers was a rally series which was run from 1970 to 1972. Car manufacturers such as Porsche, Renault, Opel and Ford took part in this competition, with Ford having an exceptionally successful year in 1972.

programme.title: Mercedes 300 SL Lightweight
programme.desc: An iconic racing car and one of only 29 ever built! We accompanied the Mercedes 300 SL 'lightweight' on its premiere drive at the Mille Miglia.

programme.title: Bentley Mulsanne EWB
programme.desc: The long version of the Bentley Mulsanne is a prime example of a chauffeured limousine. With it, the British luxury car brand has set the bar extremely high when it comes to automotive comfort.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Since the 1950s, the Mercedes-Benz SL has been regarded as the sports car legend par excellence. Beginning with the legendary 300 SL with its gullwing doors, the SL series stands for innovation and cultivated sportiness.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The Ford Mustang is the icon of all sports coupes and convertibles - no other car conveys so much the lifestyle of the 1960s. With its striking shape and powerful engines the Mustang drove itself into the hearts of millions.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: The Beatles, Peter Sellers, Britt Ekland or the British royals, they all drove the Austin Mini. Designed on a napkin, the Mini starts an incredible career in 1959: the revolutionary Mini is considered the prototype of all small cars.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: A car that everyone knows and that almost everyone has ridden in, a car that has conquered all continents and bears an unmistakable nickname, the Volkswagen Beetle.

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Ferrari - the name alone raises the pulse. No other sports car has as much magic and myth as the fiery red icons from Maranello. Whether on the road or on the race track, these cars are the centre of attention.

programme.title: Facel Vega Facellia
programme.desc: In the late 1950s, the Facel Vega Facellia was designed to compete with Porsche and Alfa Romeo and open a new market segment for the fledgling French luxury car company.

programme.title: Saab 93 and Saab 99 Turbo
programme.desc: In 1937 an airplane manufacturing company was founded in Sweden that later became the famous car manufacturer Saab. We present two of their iconic car models, the Saab 93 and 99 Turbo.

programme.title: Beradino
programme.desc: A „bella macchina“, a beautiful car - but not designed by masters like Bertone or Pininfarina. Johannes Paulussen from Neuss in Germany built the Beradino by hand.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: Normal is not enough. Tuning is a way of life for many car fans - the search for ever more horsepower, better sound and extraordinary design.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: The Monza Rally Show is a classic among drift shows. Plus: a Mercedes G-Class becomes a special off-roader 'ORC Bull'. And: a Mini Countryman becomes a Dakar Rally competitor.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: Porsche is like a religion! The faiths: Punk, technology and racing. Porsche punk Magnus Walker preaches individualism for historic vehicles. Technology has been embodied by Alois RUF since 1983. And for the racers, there is the GT3 RS.

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: BMW tries to combine the electric future with fuel-saving features in the i8. In addition: the 'Race Chip' is tested on a 3,000-kilometre route. And: What is the benefit of the switchable performance enhancement from DTE Systems?

programme.title: Tuning
programme.desc: They are the US car icons par excellence: Chevy, Ford Mustang and Corvette. At Race 61, fans of historic racers pay homage to their heroes. And: we explore the history of the Ford Mustang up to the current model.

programme.title: Volvo Laplander 6x6

programme.title: Streetwise

programme.title: Streetwise
programme.desc: The 'little' Mercedes-Benz S250 with a four-cylinder engine needs so little fuel that one could call this car a piggybank. Also: the power packages Nissan 370 Z and Wiesmann GT MF5. And: the ADAC Eco Test.

programme.title: Going Beyond
programme.desc: Going Beyond is wanderlust-filled hitchhiker Mariia Khandus’s new travel project. She’s journeyed around the world. Everybody knows that Thailand, Vietnam, and Indonesia are great places to relax with wonderful beaches and delicious fruits! But what do you know about the local people? The expats? About the real lives of those living in these exotic countries? In our trip, we will discover it all, together! We visit the non-touristy places and show you the real Indochina! This is a set of stories of different people, through the prism of whom we show life in a country. It is a collection of diverse achievements, experiences and emotions. We are looking for the most interesting stories for you to keep expanding your own consciousness. Unbelievable panoramic views, interesting people, exciting stories and adventures – you’ll see all of this in our travel show, Going Beyond!

programme.title: Basin and Range Trail Thru Hike
programme.desc: The Basin and Range Trail is a spectacular 1090 mile thru-hiking route across central Nevada’s Basin and Range country, better known as the Great Basin. The Basin and Range Trail, an original long distance hiking route created by Eric Poulin, showcases some of the best hiking Nevada has to offer, along with some of the toughest. Hiking the Great Basin means hiking off-trail, bushwhacking, along game trails. Unlike the well-blazed trails of the AT, PCT and CDT, the Basin and Range Trail is a different kind of thru hike.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Drill Charging Station
programme.desc: Back in 2010 I built a Drill Charging Station to show off a new joinery gadget. It was really simple and didn't quite have a feature set outside of being two shelves on the wall. So only eight short years later I finally decided to build a proper Drill Charging Station, made from Baltic Birch plywood featuring all the storage I need for 5 drills, two chargers, and all of my bits and accessories.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: DIY Kids School Desk - Quick - Easy - Inexpensive!
programme.desc: A one-day build using 1/4 sheet of plywood and a 2x4.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Knock Down Trestle Table Part 1
programme.desc: The table is a trestle design which keeps the legs out of the way and gives us plenty of overhang. The joinery is all mortise and tenon including some cool double wedged mortise and tenon joints. I even added extra supports in the middle of the table that will not only support the top but should also help keep the table top flat over time.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Woven Panel Rolling Hamper Part 2
programme.desc: The hamper is assembled, hinges are added, casters are attached, finish is applied, and snaps are installed on the cotton bags.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Tricked Out Bandsaws Featuring Carter Products
programme.desc: The bandsaw is one of my favorite tools and if you treat it well, it will quickly become one of your favorites as well. While most modern bandsaws come with decent components, to begin with, there are companies like Carter Products who make high-quality after-market add-ons that can make your bandsaw better performing and easier to adjust. One of the best upgrades you can do is replacing the guide

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Cutting Thin Strips at the Table Saw
programme.desc: Resawing thin stock and cutting thin strips is typically the domain of the bandsaw. And while I consider the bandsaw to be an essential shop tool, not everyone has one. So it's probably worth considering an alternative option that kills two birds with one stone: utilizing a more common tool that results in a smoother cut.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Protecting Outdoor Furniture with Epoxy Feet
programme.desc: Mother Nature always wins. So when you make outdoor furniture you have two choices: commit to a regular maintenance schedule or come to terms with the weathered gray look. An easy thing you can do to help the cause is to prevent moisture from entering into the legs. This simple trick requires nothing more than epoxy and masking tape.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Trestle Table Part 2
programme.desc: Now that the leg pieces are cut to their rough shape, we need to focus on blending the parts using an assortment of tools including a router, a ball mill, and a cabinet-maker’s rasp. You’ll notice that much of the sculpting work is done before the glueup. I find it much easier to work on these parts in smaller pieces rather than trying to work the entire finished leg at once.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: AWFS 2007 Special - Part 1 of 2

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Bit Storage Cabinet
programme.desc: A wall-hanging cabinet to help you organize and store your drill and router bits.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: 60 Seconds to Sharp
programme.desc: Most videos about sharpening, including my own, focus on how to tune up an old tool or properly set a new one. Thankfully, once you do that process it isn't likely you'll have to do it again for a very long time. From that point on, you'll be sharpening in maintenance mode.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: You Don't Need Breadboard Ends - Ask TWW
programme.desc: You don't need breadboard ends - and that's why.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Urea Resin Woodworking Glues
programme.desc: We take a look at urea resin woodworking glues. These glues definitely have their advantages: low water content, gap-filling, long open time, and rigid glue lines just to name a few. But keep in mind the one big disadvantage: safety. These glues are pretty nasty and you might be best served considering other options. But with proper precautions, this glue can be a nice addition to your shop.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Making Raised Panel Doors aka Raising Arizona

programme.desc: Thoughts on Grizzly's planes? Coping Sleds. Problem with Tung Oil Finish. Fesool Sanders 3 vs 5 Stroke How to Soundproof the Shop. What are your greatest influences? Glue for Vacuum Pressing. Filling Epoxy Gaps Is Carbon Filtration Helpful? Is CNC a novelty?

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: VerySuperCool Tools After-Market Tablesaw Fence
programme.desc: The guys over at VerySuperCool Tools recently gave me an opportunity to test out one of their new products: an after-market fence system. The great thing about this unit is that it works perfectly with existing Biesemeyer-style fences. So installation is as simple as dropping it on the rail and performing a standard fence calibration.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A Better Way to Apply Oil Finishes!
programme.desc: Applying oil finishes sparingly is the key to avoiding problems with curing and other flaws in the surface.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Rubbing Out a High Gloss Finish
programme.desc: One of the biggest challenges woodworkers face is getting a nice smooth blemish-free finish. It's to be expected that our finish will nearly always have dust and other pieces of debris residing within it. Fortunately, there is a way that just about any finish can be improved.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew relies on a jerkbait from late fall through the spawn whether using electronics or not. He keeps two color options: translucent for sunny or clear water and solid for cloudy or stained conditions.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt highlights how different SPRO Aruku Shad versions and hook sizes enhance performance based on season cover and action. He adjusts for fall rates with yo-yo or straight retrieves and downsizes when the bite is tough.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock relies on burning a crankbait over grass rock and stumps during late winter and pre-spawn. He ups his line size to keep the bait higher and uses a 7'4" rod for longer casts and ripping it free from grass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Robert Gee
programme.desc: Robert Gee reflects on his 2024 success with largemouth smallmouth and spotted bass noting that spots and smallmouth chase differently than largemouth requiring presentation adjustments. He shares his preferred head sizes go-to knot and a simple rod and reel setup most anglers can use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Emil Wagner
programme.desc: Emil Wagner sheds light on his favorite bait for winter fishing especially on spotted bass lakes like Lanier. With jig head minnows neko rigs and dropshots becoming popular everyone forgot about the shaky head.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin sets up the calendar for Florida's Spawn Cycle. Depending on weather spawn can start in south Florida as early as Thanksgiving week and extend through May of the next year. Martin gives his take on the difference of a lake like Okeechobee and the St. Johns River farther north.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen explains his two-pronged approach at the St. Johns River sticking to one area for four days using a black and blue swim jig and a flipping jig. He highlights his swim jig cadence and the importance of his flipping jig falling into hard cover

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: Brandon Palaniuk shares the three baits he used to win the Bassmaster Elite Series at Lake Okeechobee: a Megabass Kanata jerkbait and two Megabass crankbaits (Big M and a prototype). Fishing one spot aggressively led to some of the biggest strikes seen on Bassmaster LIVE.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock discusses the rising trend of using a swimbait in the prespawn as a substitute for commonly thrown baits with similar profiles. Fished around the same shallow cover it can trigger the big kicker bite tournament anglers seek.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson provides a solution to those tricky bass that are days from spawning and sit high in the water column. Not only does a jig provide great opportunities for good catches but a swimbait also entices those big females to commit.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Easton Fathergill
programme.desc: Easton Fothergill gives his daily adjustment to how fish were positioned each day of the Classic. From windy days to calm moments Fothergill kept adjusting his tackle to maximize efficiency.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey goes through what he would consider his spring selection for largemouth fishing. Spring means March and April in the south but can mean April May and June up north. Downey opts for a crankbait swim jig and two types of soft plastics when making the spring transition.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen goes through two baits he always has rigged up this time of year. A tube and a jig are staples in Lowen's boat and he explains how both get fished in conjunction with one another. There are a few variables like pegging his weight or letting it free flow and also line size in these situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher breaks down his single bait that produced a record winning margin and over 118 pounds of bass at the Pasquotank River. Flipping a Rapala CrushCity Bronco Bug to shallow roamers and spawning bass was his strategy. He utilized his forward facing sonar to pick out fish among the cover littered on the bottom.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: The Shad Spawn is a unique stage of the fishing season that bridges the gap from the bass spawn into the post spawn. Shad spawning around hard shallow cover gives bass a great opportunity to feed heavily in a short window of time. Not all places in the country feature a shad spawn but if threadfin are present in your lake a shad spawn is likely to happen. Low-light conditions early in the morning are helpful and baits like a spinnerbait imitate small shad perfectly to load the boat for Greg Hackney in a hurry.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Paul Marks
programme.desc: Paul Marks shows off his single bait that produced in two different situations depending on how he rigged it. The Zoom Fluke Stick in Natural Shad contributed almost all of his weight in his Elite victory at Lake Hartwell. His first approach was rigging it weightless to throw on shallow points where bass pushed blueback herring to feed in the morning then he switch to a shakey head in the afternoons.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses the tricky period immediately after bass leave the bed and are either guarding fry or recovering from the spawn. Here is how Christie opts to catch them.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tucker Smith
programme.desc: Tucker Smith talks about finding hard spots on Lake Fork with his side imaging throughout practice and then using his forward facing sonar to execute and catch fish throughout the tournament. He utilized a 7-inch minnow on spinning tackle with varying head sizes as well as a 3/4-ounce football jig on the final day.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Pat Schlapper
programme.desc: Pat Schlapper recounts his finest tournament week to date where to took the title at the Sabine River. Schlapper relied on a few areas of the Sabine along with a few lures including a Do-It Molds compact jig he pours himself altering it with a smaller stouter hook. He also utilized a Brazalo Custom Lures Bushwhacker Buzz Bait in the morning on the final day when it put multiple quality fish in the boat.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes tackles where the fish go when they finish spawning but the water temperatures aren't at their hottest yet like they will be later in the summer. Cifuentes dives into three different baits that are useful around lakes with standing timber for the last week of May as we head into June.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Florida pro Bernie Schultz talks buzzbaits specifically two kinds. He keeps a squeaking buzzbait and clacking buzzbait ready to go at all times especially in the post-spawn. Although it's an excellent technique in the post-spawn Schultz acknowledges its use early in the year in places like Florida Texas and other southern states. Buzz it slow or fast make it clack or squeak add a toad or a trailer hook whatever you'd like with a buzzbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock explains a new bait he was introduced to that helps him catch not only deep northern smallmouth but also southern largemouth in the winter months. He also discusses the value in 2D sonar with this technique around structure in the south.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Roberston
programme.desc: Matt Robertson talks about upsizing his spinnerbait and adjusting his blade sizes when throwing this lure in water temperatures varying from the 40's to 50's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Austin Felix
programme.desc: Austin Felix gives his thoughts on when he picks up a Dropshot versus a Ned Rig and a Neko Rig. Speed is often the determining factor for each presentation and he tends to reserve the Neko for largemouth situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew talks about one of his favorite fun-fishing lures which is the Umbrella Rig aka Alabama Rig. LeHew utilizes this in multiple ways as he can cover water around shallow cover like he would with a spinnerbait but also with his electronics around deeper offshore structure.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New goes through some of the keys he likes in his jig when targeting bass in the prespawn. New breaks down his jig trailer and why it's efficient and also explains an adjustment to his jig size that he used to never use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher gives his take on a few productive lures in the prespawn and how he balances their uses to be most effective while on the water. Should you use a Chatterbait where a jig could also work or vice versa he attacks this and more in this scenario.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Card
programme.desc: Brandon Card gives his thoughts on early season jerkbait fishing. Card gives scenarios when he will opt for a different cadence for his jerkbait rod length and line size.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Todd Auten
programme.desc: Todd Auten goes over three Chatterbait variations that have made the South Carolina pro successful with this technique. Whether it's color selection trailer options or getting the bait to ride high in the water column or fall fast Auten has his process. 1. White/CChartuese w/Zoom Shimmer Shad 2. Black/Blue w/Zoom ZCraw or Green Pumpkin Fluke 3. Firecraw w/Speed Craw

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyoya Fujita
programme.desc: Kyoya Fujita gives the specifics of his lures that helped him win at Toledo Bend. Fujita was using a technique called "mid-strolling" to get his Jackall Drift Fry and his Deps Sakamata Shad to the correct depth to target suspended bass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Trey McKinney
programme.desc: Lake Fork Champion Trey McKinney gives his lure arsenal as he adjusted daily to the changing fish for the second stop of the Elite Series season. Early in the event he used a jerkbait and jig head minnow combo but as the weather warm and conditions changed his baits adapted. Culminating on the final day were multiple baits contributed to his 130-15 tournament weight.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brad Whatley
programme.desc: Brad Whatley gives his strategy of covering water around the spawn when there is thicker cover present. Whatley winds his weighted swimbait around spawning areas and will trigger strikes or boils revealing where bass are positioned to catch on another tactic if necessary.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kenta Kimura
programme.desc: Kenta Kimura gives some suggestions to be better with the Megabass Magdraft swimbait. He changes the treble to his signature Ryugi quad-hook design for better hookups and he also adds a split ring to the line tie for increased head action and roll. Those two things are essential for Kimura along with finding the right speed on retrieve.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Hamner
programme.desc: Justin Hamner gives his strategy to catch key bass each day of competition and how he utilized multiple kinds of jerkbaits and mixed in a jig to catch the majority of his weight on Grand Lake in the 2024 Bassmaster Classic.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Bernie Schultz gives his three trusted lures when he is covering water to develop a pattern in the spring. He balances a spinnerbait swim jig and chatterbait when he approaches different types of cover.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Patrick
programme.desc: Kyle Patrick gives his approach for fishing for less pressured fish during the spawning months of the year. The fishing myth around the spawn is that bass have to go to the bank to do their yearly spawn when in reality fish can spawn much deeper and will take longer to do so.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Garrett
programme.desc: John Garrett runs down the three baits that were key for his win on the Harris Chain of Lakes. Garrett rotated between these techniques depending on how the fish were positioned and their aggressiveness on the shell bar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston goes over his two main lures for bed fishing at the St. Johns River en route to his first Elite Series victory. Johnston also explains his use of Perspective Mode when seeing bed fish in low visibility times.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Caleb Sumrall
programme.desc: Caleb Sumrall talks about one of the best ways to catch big bass. Sumrall strongly believes in a frog but when bass start shying away or missing it he downsizes instead of changing baits completely. When conditions change bass moods can vary and with that topwater becomes a high risk high reward situation and Sumrall will downsize to the keep the odds in his favor.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Seth Feider
programme.desc: Seth Feider goes through his wood jig and grass jig setup. He explains the differences in line tie and weed guard why he likes a short hook and his colors for flipping. Whether it's docks laydowns shoreline grass or submerged vegetation; Feider will often rely on a jig to get it done. His favorite size is a 5/8 ounce.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Patrick Walters
programme.desc: Elite Series Champion Patrick Walters gives the details of his approach at Lake Murray. Walters relied on a few baits throughout the week to win the event wire to wire. When fish were active and schooling Walters utilized a Zoom Super Fluke and a Rapala Jowler.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube walks us through one of his favorite techniques in tournaments and fun fishing. Dube gives his take on practicing with a Glide Bait and his strategy to convert followers into fish that will commit to biting.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New lays out one of his favorite topwater presentations the Buzz Toad. Pioneered by his good friend and fellow Elite Todd Auten New likes to use this bait to imitate multiple types of forage bass will eat in the post-spawn.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Crews
programme.desc: John Crews offers a different option for enticing schooling fish to bite when it gets tough and pressured in the summer. Using a Spy Bait can offer up another look that is great for casting and mimicking baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brock Mosley
programme.desc: Brock Mosley praises the most versatile lure in bass fishing the Yamamoto Senko. He shows how you can quickly switch from fishing the Senko weightless wacky rigged to adding a weight and changing the hook positioning for a Neko Rig. This lure will get fish to bite every day of the year depending on how you rig it.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cliff Prince
programme.desc: Cliff Prince dials us in on his 1/2 ounce Chatterbait setup that helped him win the Bassmaster Elite at Wheeler Lake. He also dishes the details on his magic spot and why he thinks the morning was incredible every day for him.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Cobb
programme.desc: Brandon Cobb gives his top picks for effective baits on lakes with blueback herring. Spotted bass and largemouth will get hyper focused on blueback herring when they exist on a body of water and Cobb knows these baits will work throughout the year and not a certain specific season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Taku Ito
programme.desc: Taku Ito goes through two key baits to his Bassmaster Elite Series victory at Smith Lake. From Neko Rigging a bluegill imitating bait to dropshotting a Magnum Fuzzy Dice he managed the biggest bass and bag to win.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Parks
programme.desc: Logan Parks discusses a strategy he employed at Wheeler during his first Top 10. Varying line size can help crankbaits run different depth and retrieved faster or slower. It's something he recommends during the summer months when schools are forming offshore or have been fished for frequently.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Ed Loughran III
programme.desc: Ed Loughran, who is also a practicing attorney, notched his biggest fishing achievement by winning the Bassmaster Elite Series event at Lake Champlain. He leaned on both largemouth and smallmouth en route to his first career victory. He is the Marathon Peak Performance for the 8th event of the 2024 Elite Series season.

programme.desc: Dustin uses cool new bait to help catch finicky bass

The adventure doesn’t end there—a bonus portage into another lake offers a chance to explore uncharted waters. It’s a fitting conclusion to a season filled with the unexpected and unforgettable.

programme.title: Stoked on Fishing | A Fisherman's Paradise: Stoked on Puerto Rico
programme.desc: Join Stoked On Fishing as we embark on a thrilling 6-day fishing expedition to the enchanted Island of Puerto Rico. Nestled along the west coast, we'll be based in the charming fishing town of La Pargueta and fishing along the west coast locations of Cabo Rojo and Rincon. Get ready for an unforgettable adventure filled with wide-open offshore and inshore fishing. Stoked On Puerto Rico

We take out Okuma Fishing Tackles President Doug and John, head of product development. We also have on board Colin and his wife, Amanda from Grundens, and our friend Toby from Mag Bay Lures and Mag Bay Resort down in Baja, Mexico. This trip was absolutely nuts, with the best Blue Fin Tuna fishing we have seen in Sothern California all year.

programme.title: Destination Dive
programme.desc: On this show we highlight some of the best diving in the lower Keys. From the wreck of the Vandenberg too the beautiful reefs in Key West, this show has it all.

programme.title: Dirt
programme.desc: Hop in the float plane—a new episode of DIRT just dropped. The DIRT crew made their way to Alaska, “the land of earth, sea, and sky.” All feast, no sleep is the name of the game as Josh makes the most of Alaska’s abundant and legendary daylight alongside local guides, fishermen, and even a couple grizzlies. There’ll be plenty of time to hibernate in winter. But for now—join us—there are halibut to filet, rainforest ’shrooms to forage, and mountainside meals to cook up.

programme.title: Hard Truths of Conservation
programme.desc: With the fall of the Soviet Union, wildlife populations in Tajikistan were devastated, bringing some of their unique mountain species to the brink of extinction. With the help of funds generated through hunting, vast areas are now being conserved and protected. Dan Cabela explores this conservation success.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle and Jeff scour the rugged mountains of southern Arizona in search of the elusive Coues deer, known to hunters as the “Grey Ghost.” Through scorching sun and shifting winds, they test their skill and patience chasing one of North America’s most elusive big game animals.

programme.title: Fox Hollow Outdoors
programme.desc: Larken and Michael set out on a Florida Man adventure in part 1 of this 2 part series. Join them in the Florida keys and Everglades for an experience that few get to experience.

programme.title: Stomping Grounds
programme.desc: In this inaugural episode, host Ryan McVinney takes viewers to the outer reaches of Cape Cod, Massachusetts to meet a local group of boaters affectionately referred to as the “The Tin Boat Mafia”. This heart-warming family story of aluminum boat owners who share a love for the outdoors and nature is particularly moving during the COVID-19 pandemic. From fishing and surfing to sun bathing and collecting driftwood, this episode chronicles the group’s passion for the water and demonstrates why light-weight, easy-to-handle, shallow draft aluminum fishing boats are their vessels of choice for navigating the sandbars of Cape Cod, MA.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: Trenton makes a trip to Louisiana to fish with Theophile Bourgeois at the Cajun Vista Lodge. With an early rain delay, they took a tour of the lodge and learned about its long standing family history before hitting the water for some redfish.

programme.title: Saltwater Experience
programme.desc: Captains Tom Rowland and Rich Tudor are joined by Captain Tony Young for a day of offshore fishing and free diving out of Islamorada.

programme.title: Fox Hollow Outdoors
programme.desc: Michael and Larken head to South Texas in search of trophy-sized trout. Along the way they make a pitstop to gear up and custom-build a Texas wading rod.

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: Josh takes his friend Isaiah to the blue water as they look for destin's latest hot bite, the blackfin tuna.

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: Josh and George from Two Georges Marina battle the wind and tide on a tough day of fishing which leads Josh to fish another day, solely for revenge on the Sheepshead!

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: Join Captain Josh and Sheriff Eric Aden for a day of fishing and fun in Destin, Florida. These two friends hit the water, catching fish both offshore and inshore, and reeling in some impressive catches. With plenty of laughs, great stories, and a few surprises along the way, this episode is all about the joy of fishing and the bond between two guys who love the sea.

programme.title: Goin' Coastal
programme.desc: Join the Mayor of Destin as he ventures into the world of coastal fishing, leaving the city behind for a day of fun and unexpected challenges. With plenty of laughs and surprising twists, this episode showcases the Mayor in a whole new light.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle Green meets up with some friends at the Idaho Fish and Game Department to ice fish for cutthroat trout. Looking to test the results of previous restocking efforts, they'll be heading to some of the most remote lakes in the state only accessible by snowmobile.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle Green and Jeff Hutchinson head to Northern Maine to hunt for moose and learn about the conservation of this species which is under attack by winter ticks. Can reducing moose numbers be the key to saving the local moose population from this deadly parasite?

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle Green is joined by his childhood friends in his home state of Michigan for a trout fishing adventure. They visit the most dynamic landmarks in the Upper Peninsula, do a little cliff jumping, and finish out the trip cooking trout riverside.

programme.title: The Green Way Outdoors
programme.desc: Kyle and Jeff dive into the wild waters off Hawaii’s coast, coming face-to-face with sharks and graceful manta rays. The adrenaline peaks when Kyle takes a heart-pounding leap off a towering 40-foot cliff, making this adventure as daring as it is unforgettable.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: Mark Peterson is in the final stretch of completing the South America Upland Slam. Having already checked off nine species in Argentina, he now finds himself in Peru, where he faces the challenge of tracking down two elusive species to complete his list: the Andean Tinamou and the Western Peruvian Dove.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: Join Mark Peterson as he embarks on a thrilling hunt in Croatia for the Eurasian Brown Bear. Experience the beauty of the Croatian wilderness and witness the skill and precision required for a successful hunt. Follow along as Mark faces all the challenges dealing with wind and a big bear that is extremely smart, making it very difficult to harvest this amazing animal. Don’t miss this exciting hunting adventure with Mark Peterson in Croatia!

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: In this episode, Mark Peterson finds himself deep in the heart of Peru and focuses on completing the prestigious South America Upland Slam. With only one bird remaining, the Western Peruvian Dove, the trip has led him to a private hunting property. This final challenge will take place over a cut cornfield, a favorite spot for the doves. To blend in, Mark and his team craft a makeshift blind using a mix of corn stalks, and timber, just enough cover while allowing for a clear shot. These West Peruvian Doves are known for their erratic flight patterns, often bouncing from one tree to another in a random manner, making timing and placement critical.

programme.title: The Journey Within
programme.desc: The hunt for FREAK SHOW became a thrilling adventure after I spotted him on Cabela’s trail cam. Having hunted Kentucky for over a decade and established my own properties—Bootleggers Ridge and Stonewall Plantation—I was eager for the chance at such a remarkable deer. Despite having drawn a coveted caribou tag through Worldwide Trophy Adventures’ TAGS Program, the allure of FREAK SHOW was too strong to resist. After careful planning and waiting for the right wind, I finally - set out on September 11. With my crossbow in hand, I waited anxiously in the stand, my heart racing as the shadows lengthened. Just when I thought the evening might end without a sighting, a movement caught my eye, sending my pulse soaring. With caution, FREAK SHOW appeared.

programme.title: American Heroes Outdoors

We also highlight our next SCHEELS Hometown Hero, Jim Moe! Click PLAY and check out the good things happening in North Dakota!

programme.title: American Heroes Outdoors

programme.title: The WoodHaven Way

Her father blames here for having left school too early and the family makes no effort to hide their dislike of Pierre, the would-be father, who is still a no-show. programme.title: My Zen Family - Season 1 - Welcome in a new world

An in-depth reflection which resulted in the creation of a place where one could share and transmit this method of well-being. Euphoria Retreat is a clever blend of Taoist and Hellenic philosophy based on the symbolism of the five elements: water, wood, fire, earth and metal. This historic place of well-being offers exclusive medical-scientific therapies combining the healing properties of water with advances in Western medicine and alternative medicines. Upon arrival, a team of specialists carries out a targeted diagnosis to create a personalized protocol, rebalancing the mind, body and soul, with a simple promise: offering a longer and better-lived life. - A constantly evolving method, between ancestral wisdom and innovation, where the Palazzo Fiuggi medical spa presents an avant-garde wellness experience, integrating cutting-edge technologies to understand and analyze individual needs, but also to support physical regeneration. This integrative approach goes beyond the simple treatment of symptoms, seeking to heal the body, mind and soul as a whole, thus elevating the concept of spa treatment to a new level.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When Sonic and Tails are captured by Grounder and Scratch, Sonic tricks them into letting them escape by reminiscing about how they all met. Several badniks seen early on in this episode later resurfaced in Dr. Robotnik's Mean Bean Machine.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: While on pursuit with Scratch and Grounder, Sonic and Tails hide in an underground mine which a miser mole think that they are trespassers.

programme.title: Sonic TV
programme.desc: The Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog 24/7

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Sonic must save a family of sloths from Dr. Robotnik's slow-motion ray, but when he himself is slowed down by Scratch and Grounder, Tails and the sloth family must take action.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Desperate to get workers to build a Robotnik statue, Dr. Robotnik opens Casino Night Zone with his pal Smiley but when Sonic stops Scratch and Grounder, Robotnik traps Tails so Sonic has to make a choice to save his pal.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik imprisons a satirical cartoonist named Sketch Lampoon for making fun of him in his comic book, much to the anger of Sonic, his biggest fan. Sonic purposely allows his own capture as well, but does not expect to be placed in a maximum-security jail cell. With Robotnik angrily sends Sonic in the cell for interfering with his plans once again.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Scratch, Grounder and Coconuts set up a chili-dog trap which then resulted with Tails been captured by a mysterious person so Sonic has to find Tails and for Robotnik and co to capture Sonic.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: While Scratch and Grounder try to catch Sonic using a Suction plate, two aliens, one being a prince, crash lands on Mobius. Sonic meets the prince when he finds out that the prince's baby brother would blow up Mobius which Sonic must save.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik's momma escapes from the home for mothers of villains and demands her birthday present! When she endangers Sonic and Tails, and they manage to have her taken back to the home, even Robotnik is glad to see her go.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Coconuts is exiled by Robotnik to a remote jungle, where he uses a giant baby ape to destroy villages. But Sonic exposes Coconuts as a robot, and the baby ape's real Dad takes Coconuts and the baby ape away for a spanking.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: A country and western singer released a song about Sonic which is making Dr. Robotnik mad and builds a music destroyer robot.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: An energetic salesman named Wes Weasley sells Robotnik numerous gadgets to help Scratch and Grounder capture Sonic. However, Robotnik later comes to regret it when Weaseley's gadgets keep backfiring.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Sonic and Tails rescue Lucas, Robotnik's first prisoner, and attempt to reunite him with his girlfriend, Lucinda. However, Robotnik is also in love with Lucinda, and pursues Lucas.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: En route to stop a train of explosives from arriving at Robotnik's munition factory, Sonic and Tails must deal with a duo of bears named Big Griz and Big Mike after Scratch and Grounder tell them that Sonic and Tails are the enemies.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik takes Professor Von Schlemmer hostage and uses his growth machine to try and enlarge himself. However, the machine backfires, and enlarges Tails instead in nearby Wienerville. Sonic must keep the famished Tails from getting into more danger as Robotnik tricks the citizens into thinking that Sonic is the villain, while Robotnik is the hero planning to save the city.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When Sonic decides to find Tails a suitable foster home to ensure his safety, Robotnik finds out and creates a robot fox family, who pose as Tails' long-lost parents.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When overweight, elderly superhero Captain Rescue bungles in his attempts to help Sonic, he grows tired of his incompetence. Robotnik then uses Captain Rescue to successfully imprison Sonic in an impenetrable force field, and Tails and Captain Rescue must save him.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Scratch suffers a blow to the head and believes that he is his favorite television character, Edgar Eagle. Sonic uses this to his advantage in preventing another of Robotnik's schemes.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: There is a Sonic Appreciation Day happening where Sonic is the guest in a hotel. However, someone steals his power sneakers and now Sonic and Tails have to find the culprit.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Tails adopts a cute and fuzzy pet named Walter who turns out to be a black hole who sucks up everything in Mobius. Realizing that Walter is from another dimension our heroes have to return him and they soon find themselves spinning through interdimensional limbo.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When Robotnik opens up a resort to make the resident Mobians his slaves, Sonic enlists the help of some robots from an area of Mobius called Scrap Valley.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik creates a robot Sonic suit with the intent of ruining the hedgehog's reputation. He forces a lab rat named Laurence to pilot by threatening his parents.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Dr. Robotnik creates a genius chip so he would have enough brains to rule Mobius, however a computer hacker got hold of it which then the chip landed inside Grounder causing him to be smart.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Sonic leaves Tails in charge of protecting a squirrel village food supply, when he zips off to stop a dam from breaking. Robotnik sends Scratch and Grounder after Tails, who defends himself the best he can with Home Alone booby traps for Scratch and Grounder. When Tails is finally caught, Sonic speeds back to save him.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik introduces the Ultra Freeze-O-Matic, announcing his plan to freeze every citizen on Mobius so that he can install Servitude Chips into the frozen citizens and make them unquestionably obedient. Sonic and Tails must foil the scheme.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When Robotnik invades Labyrinth, an underwater city, and kidnaps Princess Bubbles, a seahorse-dude named Surff seeks Sonic's help. It seems Surff and the Princess are in love, but the royal family deems Surff unworthy. Sonic, Tails and Surff must avoid the undersea traps and Mobius sea monsters while Sonic rescues the Princess and reunites her with Surff -- making it look like Surff did the whole thing.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik reprograms a machine created by Von Schlemmer capable of turning dreams into reality, unleashing a Nightmare Monster upon Mobius.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When S and G rocket to outer space to mine a radioactive mineral from asteroids, Sonic and Tails stow away. Through a blunder by the robots, all are stranded in space, and Robotnik tries to blow all of them out of the stars. Sonic builds a rocket out of S and G's spare parts, and all return to Mobius.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik's attempt to turn Sonic into an old man with his newest device backfires, turning him and Tails, and later himself, into babies. Now stuck in a day-care, the infantile Sonic and Tails must try to keep Robotnik under control, while Scratch and Grounder attempt to get him back.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik plans to block out the sun and extinguish all life and nature on the planet Mobius. Then he creates a robot son and tries to train him in the ways of wickedness. But when Robotnik Jr. meets Sonic, he becomes a naturalist and teams up with Sonic to thwart Robotnik's evil scheme.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik invents an electron altering generator which makes Scratch and Grounder twice as fast as Sonic. When they lose it and Tails picks it up, Tails speeds through the Mobius countryside leaving disasters and accidents in his wake. Seeing this, Robotnik convinces the villagers that the little fox belongs in jail, and Tails is forced to flee. With Tails all alone, Scratch and Grounder attack, and Sonic makes a last minute rescue.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik captures a Kangaroo named MacHopper, and uses his brain-wipe-reprogramming-computer to transform him into a resourceful demolitions expert (Ala MacGiver). But Mac escapes before Robotnik installs the final Get Sonic program, and teams up with Sonic and Tails to BLAST Robotnik.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Sonic joins up with a group of Dr. Robotnik's rejects who have been banished to the dump and helps them understand that their shortcomings were really their strengths.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: When S and G rocket to outer space to mine a radioactive mineral from asteroids, Sonic and Tails stow away. programme.desc: When a Rebel Base is threatened by Robotnik, Sonic and Tails team up with Big Mike and Da Bears to run a booby-trapped gauntlet in their gigantic Road Warrior-like truck, breaking through every obstacle S and G put in their way until they save the rebels.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik pretends to retire, and lures Sonic and Tails into a phony vacation resort, laden with booby-traps set by Scratch and Grounder. But Sonic takes the bungee jumping, hang gliding, and skydiving in stride, and gives the bashes the bots.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Robotnik and a rival named Quark Rex try to cooperate in capturing Sonic. However, Sonic tricks them into becoming enemies, and they try to outdo each other.

programme.title: Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog
programme.desc: Coconuts acquires a magic wand and magical gadgets from Wes Weasley (after agreeing to forward all payments to Robotnik), and attempts to master them. Meanwhile, Robotnik tries to change Sonic-themed mobium banknotes into Robotnik banknotes in the Mobius Mint.
